input.edge_amputations: "Wide" keeps the entire obelisk fully within frame with generous margin on all sides — a safe, uncommitted crop. "Tight" also keeps the obelisk whole but pushes it closer to the top edge, tightening the headroom intentionally to emphasize height, while the ground plane is cropped consistently in both.
input.incidental_distractions: "Wide" is a clean, empty scene with no additional elements. "Tight" introduces a small standing figure (tripod-like silhouette with a round head) near the base to the right of the monument, adding a human/scale reference absent in the wide shot.
input.subject_placement: In "wide," the obelisk sits dead-center, splitting the frame symmetrically with a lot of empty sky above and around it. In "tight," the monument is shifted left of center, landing closer to the left third-line, which opens up negative space on the right for the human figure — a more deliberate, dynamic composition.
input.tiebreaker: The bystander figure in "tight" acts as the story element — a scale reference and implied human presence that beats the cleaner but emptier "wide" frame, per the rubric's tiebreaker rule.
